titulo: Passato remoto (for reading): The regular endings

aula.objetivo: Recognise and read the passato remoto, the tense of stories, history books, biographies and novels. Learn the regular endings, especially the third person singular and plural, the most common irregular verbs, and the use of «nel» with a year. Avoid the English-speaker traps: leaving out the accent in «chiamò» and «partì», using the singular ending with «loro», and «in» before a year.

blocos.titulo: The passato remoto: the regular endings
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: the passato remoto tells finished events that are distant in time. It is the usual tense of novels, short stories, biographies and history books, so the aim of this lesson is to recognise it and read it with confidence. STEP 2: in everyday speech it depends on the region. It is less common in much of the north and still natural in many parts of the south and in Sicily. STEP 3: the endings of verbs in «-are» are «-ai, -asti, -ò, -ammo, -aste, -arono»: «chiamò» (called), «lasciò» (left), «arrivò» (arrived), «bussò» (knocked), «arrivarono» (they arrived). STEP 4: the endings of verbs in «-ire» are «-ii, -isti, -ì, -immo, -iste, -irono»: «partì» (left), «uscì» (went out), «seguì» (followed), «aprì» (opened). STEP 5: verbs in «-ere» have «-ei (or -etti), -esti, -é (or -ette), -emmo, -este, -erono (or -ettero)», but many common «-ere» verbs are irregular, as the next session shows. STEP 6: the written accent matters. «Chiamò» is the passato remoto, third person singular, while «chiamo» is the present, first person singular. «Partì» is not the same as «parti». STEP 7: the third person singular and plural are the forms you will meet most often in a story, so learn them first.
blocos.comparacao: English has one simple past for everything: «he called», «they arrived», «he left». Italian has the passato prossimo for everyday speech and the passato remoto mainly for narration, and in speech the choice depends on the region. English has no written accents, so learners often leave them out and write «chiamo» for «chiamò». And because the English past never changes with the person, they may also use the singular ending with a plural subject.

exemplos.ru: Il re chiamò i suoi cavalieri

erros.errado: Il re chiamo i suoi cavalieri
erros.certo: Il re chiamò i suoi cavalieri
erros.motivo: Without the accent «chiamo» is the present for «io». The third person singular of the passato remoto ends in «-ò».
The third person singular of verbs in «-ire» ends in «-ì», with a grave accent.
A plural subject such as «loro» needs the plural ending «-arono».

itens.enunciado: Which sentence is the passato remoto of «chiamare» for «il re»?
opcoes: Il re chiamò i suoi cavalieri
Il re chiamo i suoi cavalieri
Il re chiamerò i suoi cavalieri
itens.gabarito: Il re chiamò i suoi cavalieri
itens.explicacao: The third person singular ends in «-ò».

itens.enunciado: Which sentence has the right ending for a plural subject?
Which verb form is the passato remoto of «partire» for «il mugnaio»?
itens.explicacao: The ending is «-ì», with an accent.

itens.enunciado: Il re ___ i suoi cavalieri. (called, passato remoto)
itens.explicacao: The third person singular of «-are» verbs ends in «-ò».

itens.enunciado: Put in order: «Un giorno il mugnaio partì»
itens.explicacao: The time, the subject and then the verb.

blocos.enunciado: Read the story words aloud: «c'era una volta», «poi», «infine». Then say four sentences about a king, with the passato remoto of «chiamare», «arrivare», «partire» and «uscire».
Say aloud the endings «-ò», «-ì» and «-arono» and one verb for each.
